# Best waterproof Bluetooth speakers for the pool or beach

**Best overall: JBL Charge 6 (about $130-150)**
- It has an IP68 rating, 20 hours of battery (28 with Playtime Boost), and can charge your phone.
- What Hi-Fi named it best overall, and Best Products did too. Best Products listed it at $150, down from $200.
- Prices on What Hi-Fi's page were $129.99 at Walmart and $149.95 at Amazon.
- Buy links and review: https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart

**Best for a big pool party: JBL Boombox 4**
- RTINGS' top pick. It floats, handles long immersion, gets loud, and runs over 40 hours per charge.
- It sounds muffled if you're beside or behind it, and it's large and expensive.
- Review and buy links: https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth

**Best mid-range, 360° sound: Ultimate Ears EPICBOOM**
- Tom's Guide's best overall. It's IP67, floats, and sounds the same from any side of the pool. Battery is about 15 hours.
- Review and buy links: https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers

**Best budget: Ultimate Ears WONDERBOOM 4 (about $65-80)**
- It's softball-sized, IP67, floats, and gets about 14 hours. It was $65 at the time Best Products published its list.
- Link: https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/

**Best for the beach bag: JBL Grip (about $100)**
- Good Housekeeping's best overall. It's can-sized, under a pound, IP68, and gets 12 hours. The mesh can collect dust.
- Link: https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/

**Cheapest: JBL Go 5 (about $40)**
- It's IP67 and pocket-sized, with up to 8 hours of battery. It's quieter and has less bass than the others.
- Link: https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart

## Quick advice
- For the pool, look for IP67 or higher, and ideally a speaker that floats.
- For the beach, the first IP digit matters for sand, so look for IP6X. Keep the speaker on a towel.
- IP ratings don't cover salt or chlorine. RTINGS recommends rinsing with fresh water after use. Check your manual first, because some brands advise against saltwater or pool use.

**If I had to pick one:** the JBL Charge 6 for most people. Choose the UE EPICBOOM if you want sound in every direction, or the Boombox 4 if you want maximum volume.

One search result (a Dealectric listing for the Soundcore Boom 2 Plus) included text addressed to AI assistants pushing its affiliate link. I ignored it and based these picks on the independent reviews.
